instruction: Library suite completion. Open `/opt/blender/blender` first; Bonsai is available inside it as the installed BIM extension. Open the provided /home/user/Desktop/init.ifc IFC4 model in Bonsai and use it as the starting project. The init model is a simple editable seed, so keep its project structure where practical while adding, renaming, splitting, or replacing spaces and BIM elements as needed. Use Bonsai's native IFC authoring workflow and save the only required deliverable as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc using Bonsai's IFC save/export controls. The saved IFC must contain exactly four real IfcSpace objects with these exact names: Reading Room, Service Desk, Archive, and WC. Reading Room is the reader area, Service Desk is the staffed library service area, Archive is the records room, and WC is a separate space; these names identify rooms rather than furniture. Model the building as a rectangular single-storey shell about 14 m by 8 m with walls about 3.2 m high and one floor slab. Include at least 8 wall-like IfcWall or IfcWallStandardCase elements, at least 1 IfcSlab, at least 4 IfcDoor elements, and at least 5 IfcWindow elements. Create real IFC/BIM elements rather than ordinary Blender mesh placeholders or visual-only geometry. The exported IFC should use the IFC4 schema and have unique GlobalId values for IfcRoot objects. The shaped model should have an overall size roughly matching the shell, with X span about 14 m, Y span about 8 m, and Z span about 3.2 m. Other coordinates, wall thicknesses, opening positions, materials, object type names, relationship nesting, property sets, and harmless exporter metadata may vary as long as the saved IFC satisfies these requirements.
